title: Psalms Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 16.

questions.question: Who does the psalmist ask to preserve him because he puts his trust in Him?
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks God to preserve him because he puts his trust in God, as stated in Psalms 16:1.

questions.question: According to Psalms 16:2, what does the soul say to the LORD?
questions.explanation: The soul says to the LORD, 'Thou art my Lord,' as recorded in Psalms 16:2.

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 16:3, the psalmist says he delights in the saints and the excellent on earth.
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:3 states that the psalmist delights in the saints that are in the earth and the excellent.

questions.question: What will the psalmist not offer to gods other than the LORD?
questions.explanation: The psalmist says he will not offer drink offerings of blood to other gods according to Psalms 16:4.

questions.question: According to Psalms 16:4, what will happen to those who hasten after another god?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:4 says that their sorrows shall be multiplied who hasten after another god.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist declares that his goodness extends to the LORD in Psalms 16:2.
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:2 explicitly states that the psalmist's goodness does not extend to the LORD.

questions.question: In Psalms 16:1, what reason does the psalmist give for asking God to preserve him?
options: Because he puts his trust in Him
questions.correctAnswer: Because he puts his trust in Him
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks God to preserve him because he puts his trust in Him, as stated in Psalms 16:1.

questions.question: Which group does the psalmist take delight in, according to Psalms 16:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:3 identifies the saints that are in the earth and the excellent as those in whom the psalmist delights.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist says he will take up the names of other gods into his lips in Psalms 16:4.
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:4 states the psalmist will not take up the names of other gods into his lips.

questions.question: What is the psalmist's soul's attitude toward the LORD in Psalms 16:2?
questions.explanation: The soul acknowledges the LORD as Lord, as stated in Psalms 16:2.

questions.question: In Psalms 16, which comes first?
options: Not offering drink offerings of blood
questions.explanation: The first instruction or action mentioned is putting trust in God, as seen in Psalms 16:1 before other statements.

questions.question: Who is described as the portion of the psalmist's inheritance in Psalms 16:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:5 declares that the LORD is the portion of the psalmist's inheritance.

questions.question: According to Psalms 16:6, how does the psalmist describe the place where the lines have fallen to him?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:6 describes the lines as fallen in pleasant places for the psalmist.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 16:1 is a plea for preservation because the psalmist puts his trust in God.
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:1 states the psalmist asks God to preserve him because he trusts in Him.

questions.question: What does the psalmist say about his goodness in relation to the LORD in Psalms 16:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:2 says the psalmist's goodness does not extend to the LORD.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 16:5, what does the LORD represent for the psalmist?
options: His portion of inheritance and cup
questions.correctAnswer: His portion of inheritance and cup
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:5 states, 'The LORD is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup,' indicating that God is the psalmist's inheritance and sustenance. This shows trust and reliance on God rather than worldly possessions.

questions.question: How does Psalms 16:6 describe the psalmist's circumstances?
options: The lines are fallen in pleasant places; he has a goodly heritage
He walks through the valley of the shadow of death
He faces many enemies but remains strong
He is cast down but hopes in the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: The lines are fallen in pleasant places; he has a goodly heritage
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:6 declares, 'The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage,' illustrating the psalmist's grateful recognition of God's blessings and provision.

questions.question: What does the psalmist say about the counsel he receives in Psalms 16:7?
options: He blesses the LORD for giving him counsel and his reins instruct him at night
He finds counsel only among the wise elders
He ignores counsel and trusts his own understanding
He fears counsel from others but trusts only God
questions.correctAnswer: He blesses the LORD for giving him counsel and his reins instruct him at night
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:7 says, 'I will bless the LORD, who hath given me counsel: my reins also instruct me in the night seasons,' showing that God provides guidance, even in difficult or dark times.

questions.question: What is the result of the psalmist setting the LORD always before him as expressed in Psalms 16:8?
options: He shall not be moved because God is at his right hand
He will be wealthy and honored
questions.correctAnswer: He shall not be moved because God is at his right hand
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:8 says, 'I have set the LORD always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved,' indicating that steadfast faith in God brings stability and courage.

questions.question: How does Psalms 16:6-7 together teach about the importance of gratitude and divine guidance?
options: Gratitude acknowledges God's blessings and guidance comes even in difficult times
Gratitude is unimportant, but guidance is essential
Only human wisdom matters, not divine guidance
Gratitude guarantees no hardships will come
questions.correctAnswer: Gratitude acknowledges God's blessings and guidance comes even in difficult times
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:6 speaks of a 'goodly heritage' showing gratitude for God's blessings, and Psalms 16:7 highlights God's counsel and instruction at night, showing that divine guidance is continuous even in hardship.

questions.question: What biblical virtue is emphasized by the psalmist's declaration in Psalms 16:8 about keeping God always before him?
questions.explanation: By stating, 'I have set the LORD always before me,' the psalmist emphasizes unwavering faith and steadiness, showing trust that leads to being unshaken (Psalms 16:8).

questions.question: A fellow believer feels unsettled and fearful. Based on Psalms 16:5-8, what truth can you share to encourage them?
options: God is our inheritance and presence, and if we set Him always before us, we will not be moved
We must rely on our own strength to overcome fear
Material wealth is the best comfort in fear
Avoid seeking counsel because it will confuse you
questions.correctAnswer: God is our inheritance and presence, and if we set Him always before us, we will not be moved
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:5-8 teach that God is our portion and presence, giving stability and counsel, so keeping Him before us leads to courage and peace in fear.

questions.question: What will happen, according to Psalms 16:8-9, when a person sets the LORD always before them?
options: Their heart will be glad, their glory will rejoice, and their flesh will rest in hope
They will gain riches and honor
They will become popular among people
questions.correctAnswer: Their heart will be glad, their glory will rejoice, and their flesh will rest in hope
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:8-9 connects keeping the LORD before oneself with joy, gladness, and hopeful rest, showing the emotional and spiritual benefits of faith.

questions.question: According to Psalms 16:6, how does the psalmist view the inheritance God has given him?
options: As pleasant places and a goodly heritage
questions.correctAnswer: As pleasant places and a goodly heritage
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage,' showing the psalmist's grateful acceptance of God's blessings.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the role of 'reins' in Psalms 16:7 in the context of guidance?
options: Inner parts symbolizing deep emotions and conscience that instruct at night
External teachers who advise during the day
Wealth and possessions that guide decisions
Enemies that cause fear at night
questions.correctAnswer: Inner parts symbolizing deep emotions and conscience that instruct at night
questions.explanation: 'My reins also instruct me in the night seasons' refers to inner emotional or spiritual guidance God provides even in dark or difficult times (Psalms 16:7).

questions.question: How does Psalms 16:5-6 encourage believers regarding their life circumstances?
options: By trusting God as their portion, they can find contentment in their heritage and place
By seeking riches and worldly success as proof of God's favor
By relying solely on their own efforts to improve life
By isolating themselves from others to avoid hardship
questions.correctAnswer: By trusting God as their portion, they can find contentment in their heritage and place
questions.explanation: These verses teach that God is the true inheritance and that trusting Him leads to contentment with one's lot, as seen in 'The LORD is the portion of mine inheritance' and 'The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places' (Psalms 16:5-6).

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 16:5, the psalmist views God as his portion and cup, symbolizing his inheritance and sustenance.
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:5 explicitly states, 'The LORD is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup,' confirming the psalmist's view of God as his inheritance and sustenance.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 16:7 suggests that divine counsel is only available during the day when one can see clearly.
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:7 says, 'my reins also instruct me in the night seasons,' showing that divine guidance is available even during difficult or dark times.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 16:8, setting the LORD always before oneself ensures that the believer will be unshaken in life's challenges.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved,' indicating that constant awareness of God's presence gives stability.

questions.question: What does Psalms 16:5-8 teach about the relationship between trusting God and personal stability?
options: Trusting God as one's portion and presence leads to not being moved by difficulties
Trusting God means avoiding all hardships
Stability comes only from wealth and status
Personal stability is unrelated to faith
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God as one's portion and presence leads to not being moved by difficulties
questions.explanation: Verses 5-8 emphasize that when God is regarded as one's inheritance and is kept always before oneself, a believer gains steadfastness and is unshaken (Psalms 16:5-8).

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 16.

questions.question: According to Psalms 16:9, what is the state of David's heart and flesh?
options: My heart is glad and my flesh shall rest in hope
My heart is heavy and my flesh is weak
My soul is troubled and my flesh mourns
My heart is fearful and my flesh trembles
questions.correctAnswer: My heart is glad and my flesh shall rest in hope
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:9 states, 'Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope,' indicating a joyful and hopeful state.

questions.question: What does Psalms 16:10 say God will not allow to happen to His Holy One?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:10 says, 'neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption,' meaning God will not allow decay or corruption to affect His Holy One.

questions.question: In Psalms 16:11, what does the psalmist say is found in God's presence?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:11 states, 'in thy presence is fulness of joy,' indicating complete joy is found with God.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God not allowing His Holy One to see corruption as in Psalms 16:10?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:27 quotes Psalms 16:10 during Peter’s sermon, emphasizing that God would not allow His Holy One (Jesus) to undergo decay, fulfilling the prophecy.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'at thy right hand' in Psalms 16:8 and 16:11?
options: It symbolizes a place of power and protection
It refers to the east side of the temple
It indicates a place of exile
It means being ignored or neglected
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes a place of power and protection
questions.explanation: In ancient Near Eastern culture and biblical symbolism, 'at thy right hand' signifies a place of honor, strength, and protection, as referenced in Psalms 16:8 and 16:11.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Psalms 16:9 through 16:11 where the psalmist moves from personal hope to eternal joy and pleasures?
questions.explanation: The passage forms a chiasm where the psalmist’s heart gladness (verse 9) and God’s eternal pleasures (verse 11) frame the center promise of resurrection (verse 10), reflecting balanced parallelism.

questions.question: What Hebrew word translated as 'hell' in Psalms 16:10 refers to the realm of the dead?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Sheol' in Psalms 16:10 refers to the abode of the dead or the grave, often translated as 'hell' or 'the pit' in English.

questions.question: According to Psalms 16:7, when does the psalmist receive counsel and instruction?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:7 states, 'my reins also instruct me in the night seasons,' indicating guidance is received during the night.

questions.question: What does Psalms 16:5 describe as the LORD's role concerning the psalmist's inheritance?
options: The portion of my inheritance and of my cup
questions.correctAnswer: The portion of my inheritance and of my cup
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:5 says, 'The LORD is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup,' portraying God as the psalmist’s share and sustainer.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the promise in Psalms 16:11 about the 'path of life' and 'pleasures forevermore'?
questions.explanation: John 14:6 quotes Jesus saying, 'I am the way, the truth, and the life,' fulfilling the promise in Psalms 16:11 about God showing the path of life and eternal pleasures.

questions.question: Psalms 16:4 warns against following another god. What consequence does it say will come to those who do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:4 states, 'Their sorrows shall be multiplied that hasten after another god,' warning of increased affliction.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 16:8 states that because the LORD is at the psalmist’s right hand, he shall be moved.
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:8 actually says, 'because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved,' indicating stability rather than being moved.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 16:2 indicates that the psalmist acknowledges the LORD as his Lord and recognizes that his own goodness does not extend to God.
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:2 says, 'Thou art my Lord: my goodness extendeth not to thee,' showing humility and acknowledgment of God's lordship.

questions.question: What does Psalms 16:6 mean by 'The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places'?
options: God has given the psalmist a favorable portion or inheritance
The psalmist is trapped in difficult circumstances
The psalmist is wandering without direction
questions.correctAnswer: God has given the psalmist a favorable portion or inheritance
questions.explanation: The imagery of 'lines fallen' refers to land boundaries, signifying a good and pleasant inheritance as described in Psalms 16:6.

questions.question: Which Old Testament event or concept is foreshadowed by the resurrection imagery in Psalms 16:10?
options: The giving of the Law at Sinai
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:10's promise that God will not allow His Holy One to see corruption is commonly interpreted as a prophecy foreshadowing Jesus Christ’s resurrection.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 16:1 express about David's relationship with God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:1 states, 'Preserve me, O God: for in thee do I put my trust,' indicating David's reliance on God for protection and his faith in God's trustworthiness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 16:2, what does David acknowledge about his own goodness?
options: It does not extend to God
It is a reason for pride
questions.correctAnswer: It does not extend to God
questions.explanation: In Psalms 16:2, David says, 'my goodness extendeth not to thee,' recognizing that his goodness is not a contribution to God's nature or need.

questions.question: Who does David express delight in according to Psalms 16:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:3 indicates that David finds his delight in 'the saints that are in the earth, and to the excellent,' showing his appreciation for those who follow God.

questions.question: What warning does David give in Psalms 16:4 regarding those who pursue other gods?
options: They shall be multiplied in sorrows
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be multiplied in sorrows
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:4 warns that 'their sorrows shall be multiplied that hasten after another god,' indicating the spiritual consequences of idolatry.

questions.question: What does David declare the LORD to be in Psalms 16:5?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 16:5, David refers to the LORD as 'the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup,' signifying that God is his greatest treasure and source of sustenance.

questions.question: What does Psalms 16:6 suggest about David's heritage?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:6 states, 'the lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage,' indicating his gratitude for a favorable inheritance.

questions.question: According to Psalms 16:7, what does David receive from the LORD?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:7 says, 'I will bless the LORD, who hath given me counsel,' highlighting the importance of divine guidance in David's life.

questions.question: What assurance does David express in Psalms 16:8 about his relationship with the LORD?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 16:8, David states, 'because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved,' expressing confidence in God's presence and support.

questions.question: What is the result of David's gladness as stated in Psalms 16:9?
options: His heart is glad and he rejoices
questions.correctAnswer: His heart is glad and he rejoices
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:9 says, 'Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth,' indicating that David's relationship with God brings him joy.

questions.question: What assurance does Psalms 16:10 provide regarding David's soul?
options: It will be left in hell
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:10 expresses confidence that 'thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption,' indicating divine preservation.

questions.question: According to Psalms 16:11, what is found in the presence of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:11 states, 'in thy presence is fulness of joy,' emphasizing the joy that comes from being in communion with God.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 16:5 and 6 convey about God's provision?
options: God provides both inheritance and sustenance
God's provision is only for the rich
God does not provide for His people
questions.correctAnswer: God provides both inheritance and sustenance
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:5 and 6 together teach that the LORD is both 'the portion of mine inheritance' and maintains David's lot, indicating comprehensive provision.

questions.question: What does the combination of Psalms 16:9 and 10 reveal about hope after death?
options: Hope is based on personal merit
Hope is found in God's preservation
questions.correctAnswer: Hope is found in God's preservation
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:9 and 10 together reveal that David's hope is anchored in God's promise not to abandon his soul, reflecting a deep assurance in life after death.

questions.question: What does the combination of Psalms 16:3 and 4 teach about the consequences of idolatry?
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:3 and 4 illustrate that while David delights in the saints, those who pursue other gods will face multiplied sorrows, emphasizing the serious consequences of idolatry.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the Bible does not address life after death. What does Psalms 16:10 teach?
options: It is silent on the subject
It teaches that souls are abandoned
questions.explanation: Psalms 16:10 asserts, 'For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell,' affirming the belief in preservation and existence beyond death, countering sceptical claims.
